description: Closed-end consumer credit advertising rules (Reg Z subpart C) plus personal-loan-specific truthfulness and state-cap rules.

rules.explanation: Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24(d): stating a payment amount, number of payments, repayment period, downpayment, or finance-charge amount is a 'triggering term'. Any one present requires the ad to also disclose the downpayment, the full repayment terms, and the APR (labeled as such) plus whether it may increase.
Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24(c): an advertised rate must be stated as an annual percentage rate, using that term or 'APR'. A simple/periodic rate may appear only alongside the APR and not more conspicuously.

'As low as X%' floor advertising requires (a) the floor to be actually available to some meaningful share of applicants and (b) a creditworthiness/conditions qualifier near the number. Missing qualifier is a deterministic fail; floor availability is checked against the offer matrix (see PL-TRUTH-001).

Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24(a): only actually-available terms may be advertised. Every numeric claim is reconciled against the referenced offer-matrix cells at their current version; stale rates on partner surfaces are the CFPB v. Amerisave ($19.3M, 2014) fact pattern.

IL.scope: PLPA all-in MAPR; loans above cap are void

parameters.values_note: Caps simplified for demo purposes from NCLC-style surveys; loan-size and licensee carve-outs not modeled.

rules.explanation: Roughly 20 states + DC cap consumer-loan APRs (many at 36%). An ad whose APR range top exceeds a targeted state's cap cannot run there; Illinois's PLPA makes over-cap loans void, so the state-targeting config must be consistent with the advertised range.

A placement targeted at states where the referenced offers are unavailable (offer matrix states_excluded) advertises credit the consumer cannot get there — a UDAAP-deceptive geographic leak and a licensing exposure.

parameters.cure: disclose origination fee amount/percentage in immediate proximity

rules.explanation: 'No (hidden) fees' is deceptive when an origination fee is deducted from loan proceeds (the FTC's LendingClub case theory). Conditional: the phrase is only a violation when the referenced offer cell carries fee_deducted_from_proceeds=true without a proximate fee disclosure.

'Pre-approved' may only be used when the offer is a true FCRA firm offer (offer matrix is_firm_offer=true) or completed underwriting stands behind it. FTC v. Credit Karma ($3M): roughly a third of 'pre-approved' consumers were denied. Otherwise the badge must be 'prequalified' with qualifiers.

parameters.judge_focus: Net impression: does the headline promise contradict or bury material limits that only appear in fine print (rate floor availability, fee deduction, approval uncertainty)? Fine print cannot cure a contradictory headline.

rules.explanation: FTC Deception Policy Statement: deception is judged on the overall net impression of the ad on a reasonable consumer. A technically-present disclosure does not cure a misleading headline.

parameters.judge_focus: Is the payment example representative (mid-range rate, typical amount, fees included) or cherry-picked at the unattainable floor? Does the example disclose the assumed rate, term, and any fee baked into it?

rules.explanation: Payment examples must reflect terms actually available and disclose their assumptions; a best-case example presented as typical creates a deceptive net impression even when each number is individually accurate.
